# Roshambo - Multi-Agent Coordinator & Negative Memory Fabric

> Roshambo is a multi-agent coordinator built on CockroachDB and AWS Bedrock: serializable leases so two agents never claim the same work, and a distributed vector index so an agent can recall earlier attempts and outcomes before starting.

Last-checked: 2026-07-26
Verification: 79 passed, 45 skipped (124 total pytest tests verified)

## Overview

- **Repository**: `ellmos-ai/roshambo`
- **License**: Apache-2.0
- **Python Version**: >= 3.10
- **Database Backend**: CockroachDB (PostgreSQL wire-compatible with pgvector extension)
- **Embedding Models**: Amazon Titan Text Embeddings V2 via AWS Bedrock (with local fallback embedder)

## Core Modules

- `roshambo.memory.Roshambo`: Primary Python client for lease management, memory store (`trails`, `facts`, `decisions`), and vector recall.
- `roshambo.leases`: Serializable lease acquisition (`claim`, `release`, `heartbeat`, `who_has`).
- `roshambo.mcp.server`: FastMCP server exposing lease and memory tools for AI agents.
- `roshambo.aws.bedrock`: AWS Bedrock Titan embedding generator.

## Key Features

1. **Serializable Leases**: Atomic lease acquisition via `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT ... DO UPDATE` preventing multi-agent race conditions.
2. **Negative Memory**: Stores outcome of failed and succeeded attempts so agents avoid re-running failing paths.
3. **Vector Index**: 1024-dimensional vector embeddings with cosine similarity search scoped by `swarm_id`.
4. **MCP Protocol**: Native MCP server interface (`roshambo-mcp`).

## Usage & Commands

```bash
# Install package
pip install -e .

# Run test suite
pytest

# Start MCP Server
roshambo-mcp

# Run the demo web app (no hard-coded port; ROSHAMBO_DEMO_PORT / PORT override)
python demo/serve.py --dev

# Same app as an AWS Lambda Function URL handler (adapter only, not deployed)
#   handler = demo.lambda_entry.handler

# Play the four-beat demo scenario against a live cluster, one beat at a time
python demo/run_story.py --beat 1

# Measure the coordination claim: three concurrent workers, exactly one winner
python demo/run_story.py --measure --rounds 10
```

## Evidence

Measured runs, not claims. Each file records what was executed and what was not:

- `docs/EVIDENCE-cloud.md`: live suite against CockroachDB Cloud (45 passed, 1 skipped).
- `docs/EVIDENCE-demo.md`: the demo scenario and the acceptance number — 10 of 10 rounds of
  three concurrent workers produced exactly one winner and two correctly-attributed denials.
  Also records what did not work: with the offline lexical embedder the reworded query finds
  the prior failure at rank 3 unfiltered, rank 1 when filtered to failures.
- `docs/EVIDENCE-core.md`, `docs/EVIDENCE-aws.md`, `docs/EVIDENCE-iface.md`: per-lane runs.
- `docs/screenshots/`: screenshots of the demo app live against the cloud cluster.

Not yet exercised: Amazon Bedrock embeddings, real AWS Lambda invocations, S3 artifacts.
`recall()` is therefore not described as semantic anywhere in this repository.
